_comment: Carry destination for issue #1308 (R5-D2-03, the round-5 D2 audit's
sensor-drift finding; report id D2-14, judge verdict bug). The stage that
needs this is any later seat that judges or re-measures the sysid
adoption gate's confidence, or that prices sensor drift through
SystemIdentification.identify() -- a later round's D2 dimension. No
roster group in this tree claims #1308 (no wave-*-groups.json names D2,
the round-5 audit or the issue), so this file is that stage's brief.
stage: any later seat that judges or re-measures the sysid adoption gate's confidence, or that prices sensor drift through SystemIdentification.identify() (a later round's D2 dimension; tools/audit/briefs/D2.md is its method, tools/audit/round5/D2/seat-b/sysid_bias.py its round-5 harness)

carries.from: the pull request that tempers SystemIdentification.identify()'s confidence by the share of the window's movement the fitted drift could account for (R5-D2-03, #1308)
carries.control: The measurement, with the perturbation that would have falsified it. At the merge base 129f96b3 the round-5 D2 harness (tools/audit/round5/D2/seat-b/sysid_bias.py, its drift010_30min cell, 40 seeds, 0.02 C sensor noise, 30-minute cadence) admitted 6 of 40 fits at median |UA bias| 0.281 and max 0.316 against a true UA of 0.20 kW/K, and the no-drift cell (white002_30min) admitted a set at median 0.024 -- so the gate was selecting the biased fits, not rejecting them. Two nulls separate the mechanism from its imitation. (1) Removing the drift removes the effect: the same drive at 0.0 C/h fits drift ~0, its share of the movement is ~0, and the cell reads what it read before the fix. (2) The finding's own perturbation, `sensor_drift_prior_c_per_h` 0.02 -> 0.10, moves the admitted median only 0.281 -> 0.270 -- widening the ridge prior is not where the bias lives, which is why the fix discounts the confidence instead. The residual is disclosed rather than hidden: at 0.05 C/h the same harness still admits a minority at median 0.136, so the discount is a share-of-movement bound and not a drift detector.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this paragraph's numbers: they are the round-5 harness's and this branch's, and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. Run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round5/D2/seat-b/sysid_bias.py` from the repository root and read its per-cell `adopted` lines -- the drift010_30min cell must adopt nobody, and the white002_30min cell must still admit a set inside the +-10 % band. Then perturb: set the drift back to 0.0 in the cell your seat is pricing, and confirm the admitted set does not move. If a later fix changes the confidence formula again, re-derive the discount's factor by reading `identify()`'s confidence block rather than trusting the harness's cell names.
carries.brief: The sysid adoption gate's confidence now carries a drift-share discount: SystemIdentification.identify() multiplies the excursion term by `(excursion - |fitted drift| * t_span) / excursion`, so a window whose movement the fitted drift could account for does not clear the 0.3 adoption gate even when its r2, sample count, de-drifted excursion and SNR are unchanged. Two consequences for a later seat. First, do NOT read the settle cross-check in identify() as protection against sensor drift: its precondition is a fitted drift below `sensor_drift_prior_c_per_h`, and that precondition selects the honest fits (the ones the correction already pulled toward zero) and skips the biased ones -- a selection effect, not protection. Re-establish that per case, at your own merge base, before resting anything on that guard. Second, confidence is no longer a pure excitation/SNR read: a drifting window's value is also a function of how much of its movement the fitted drift explains, so two cells of a drift grid compared on `confidence` alone are comparing two different quantities. Price a drift scenario on the identified UA against the plant's true UA, and re-run the drift-share arithmetic yourself, rather than reading a confidence threshold as a drift bound -- the discount is a share-of-movement bound, and a slow enough ramp on a large enough excursion keeps a share below 1.
